newsitem.title: INDIA: India tax revenue goal is achievable - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: India tax revenue goal is achievable - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Saturday that he was confident the government would meet its tax revenue target for 1997/98 (April-March) despite proposed rate cuts.
"We're confident that we will get the revenues as projected," he told Reuters in an interview. "There is no reason why the 1997/98 budget should not achieve its target of revenues."

Chidambaram said critics had predicted that the government would fail to meet its target of reducing the fiscal deficit as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) to 5.0 percent in 1996/97 from 5.8 percent in the previous year.

"We maintained the fiscal deficit at the promised five percent. What I've projected for 1997/98 is not so ambitious," he said. The government aims to cut the fiscal deficit to 4.5 percent of GDP in 1997/98.
Chidambaram said the government was projecting that revenues from income tax, corporate tax, excise duties and customs duties would grow by 15.5 percent in 1997/98 over the current year.
"And that's quite consistent with past experience and past trends," he said.
